# Colour Key

Selects parts of your scene whose colours resemble a colour you pick.

`lfs.colour_key` · Selection

## How to use

Pick Colour, then raise Tolerance until your target is included.\
Add a little Softness to avoid a hard edge.

## Inputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Colour | `Colour` | lfs.colour | [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] | step 0.01 | RGB colour to match, usually 0–1 per channel. The default is black; pick your target colour here. |
| Tolerance | `Tolerance` | lfs.float | 0.1 | min 0; step 0.01 | Allowed RGB distance from Colour. 0 matches only that colour; 0.1, the default, allows a small variation. |
| Softness | `Softness` | lfs.float | 0 | min 0; step 0.01 | Width of the soft transition. 0, the default, gives hard edges; larger values soften the selection. |

## Outputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Selection | `Selection` | lfs.float | — | — | Selection strength: 0 is unselected, 1 fully selected; values between them make soft transitions. |
